## NVIDIA

### NVIDIA suspend and resume services {#nvidia-power-services}

Only for a driver that does not save video memory itself. nvidia-open already does, so not there

- **Guide:** [NVIDIA Driver]({{< relref "/docs/cachyos/nvidia" >}})
- **Only on:** a machine with an NVIDIA GPU
- **Marked:** Recommended
- **Source:** [the entry](https://github.com/THectic-NL/Zephyrus-Linux/blob/main/src/static/scripts/quicksetup.py#L3327-L3330) · [`on_nvidia_services`](https://github.com/THectic-NL/Zephyrus-Linux/blob/main/src/static/scripts/quicksetup.py#L1155-L1157) · [`off_nvidia_services`](https://github.com/THectic-NL/Zephyrus-Linux/blob/main/src/static/scripts/quicksetup.py#L1160-L1163)

**Turning it on**

```bash
# --- As root, one password prompt for all of it ---

# Enable the NVIDIA suspend, resume and hibernate services
systemctl enable nvidia-hibernate.service nvidia-suspend.service nvidia-resume.service
```

- nvidia-suspend-then-hibernate.service stays as it is: enable it only if you use that sleep mode.

**Turning it off (the way back)**

```bash
# --- As root, one password prompt for all of it ---

# Disable the NVIDIA suspend, resume and hibernate services
systemctl disable nvidia-hibernate.service nvidia-suspend.service nvidia-resume.service
```

- nvidia-suspend-then-hibernate.service is left alone: this never enabled it.

### NVIDIA Dynamic Boost (nvidia-powerd) {#nvidia-powerd}

Shifts the power budget between CPU and GPU. The firmware decides if it does anything, so it is optional

- **Guide:** [NVIDIA Driver]({{< relref "/docs/cachyos/nvidia" >}}#nvidia-powerd-dynamic-boost)
- **Only on:** a machine with an NVIDIA GPU
- **Source:** [the entry](https://github.com/THectic-NL/Zephyrus-Linux/blob/main/src/static/scripts/quicksetup.py#L3331-L3334) · [`on_nvidia_powerd`](https://github.com/THectic-NL/Zephyrus-Linux/blob/main/src/static/scripts/quicksetup.py#L1175-L1180) · [`off_nvidia_powerd`](https://github.com/THectic-NL/Zephyrus-Linux/blob/main/src/static/scripts/quicksetup.py#L1183-L1185)

**Turning it on**

```bash
# --- As root, one password prompt for all of it ---

# Enable NVIDIA Dynamic Boost (nvidia-powerd)
systemctl unmask nvidia-powerd.service
systemctl enable nvidia-powerd.service
systemctl start nvidia-powerd.service || echo 'nvidia-powerd did not start now (normal in Integrated mode, the dGPU is off)'
```

- The firmware decides whether Dynamic Boost does anything. asusd stops the service on battery by itself.

**Turning it off (the way back)**

```bash
# --- As root, one password prompt for all of it ---

# Disable NVIDIA Dynamic Boost (nvidia-powerd)
systemctl disable --now nvidia-powerd.service
```

### prime-run {#nvidia-prime}

Runs a program on the RTX 4060 instead of the iGPU

- **Guide:** [Proton & the Steam Linux Runtime]({{< relref "/docs/gaming/proton-slr" >}}#making-sure-the-rtx-4060-is-doing-the-work)
- **Only on:** a machine with an NVIDIA GPU
- **Marked:** Recommended
- **Source:** [the entry](https://github.com/THectic-NL/Zephyrus-Linux/blob/main/src/static/scripts/quicksetup.py#L3335-L3337)

**Turning it on**

```bash
# --- As root, one password prompt for all of it ---

# Install packages from the repositories
pacman -S --needed --noconfirm --noprogressbar nvidia-prime
```

**Turning it off (the way back)**

```bash
# --- As root, one password prompt for all of it ---

# Remove packages, one at a time (one that something else still needs is kept)
pacman -Rs --noconfirm --noprogressbar nvidia-prime
```

## AMD

### Disable AMD Panel Self Refresh {#amdgpu-psr}

Only if the system still freezes with an external monitor over USB-C or Thunderbolt. The bug was mostly on kernels 6.15 to 6.18

- **Guide:** [Known Issues]({{< relref "/docs/known-issues" >}})
- **Only on:** the Zephyrus G16 (GA605WV)
- **Marked:** `Advanced`
- **Source:** [the entry](https://github.com/THectic-NL/Zephyrus-Linux/blob/main/src/static/scripts/quicksetup.py#L3338-L3342)

This row is a guide and has no checkbox: the steps stay yours, because a mistake in them can stop the machine from booting.

**By hand, to set it up (limine)**

1. Add amdgpu.dcdebugmask=0x600 to KERNEL_CMDLINE in /etc/default/limine
2. Run: sudo limine-update
3. Reboot

**By hand, to set it up (grub)**

1. Add amdgpu.dcdebugmask=0x600 to GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT in /etc/default/grub
2. Run: sudo grub-mkconfig -o /boot/grub/grub.cfg
3. Reboot

**By hand, to set it up (systemd-boot)**

1. Add amdgpu.dcdebugmask=0x600 to LINUX_OPTIONS in /etc/sdboot-manage.conf
2. Run: sudo sdboot-manage gen
3. Reboot

**By hand, to undo it (limine)**

1. Remove amdgpu.dcdebugmask=0x600 from KERNEL_CMDLINE in /etc/default/limine
2. Run: sudo limine-update
3. Reboot

**By hand, to undo it (grub)**

1. Remove amdgpu.dcdebugmask=0x600 from GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT in /etc/default/grub
2. Run: sudo grub-mkconfig -o /boot/grub/grub.cfg
3. Reboot

**By hand, to undo it (systemd-boot)**

1. Remove amdgpu.dcdebugmask=0x600 from LINUX_OPTIONS in /etc/sdboot-manage.conf
2. Run: sudo sdboot-manage gen
3. Reboot
